Student Assistant

Imagine a future where you gain valuable work experience while helping improve global HR processes and developing your skills in data, digital tools, and process improvement

Application deadline

13 December 2026 , 23:59 CET

Country
Denmark
Location
Gentofte
Workplace
Hybrid (office and home-working) 
Working hours

Employment type
Student
Legal entity
Ørsted Services A/S

Some of our benefits include:

Proven very high employee satisfaction and motivation

Continuous development opportunities for all employees

Competitive salary, pension scheme, and attractive holiday package

A wide range of health benefits, such as health insurance, nutritious food, and fitness facilities in our office locations

Join us in this role in People & Culture, where you’ll support the smooth delivery and improvement of global HR processes. You’ll work with data, digital tools, process administration, documentation, and stakeholder support, while gaining hands-on experience of how HR processes are delivered across Ørsted.

Welcome to Global Technology & Process Management
You’ll be part of the Global Process Delivery team where you, together with your colleagues, will support our HR functions in delivering annual global HR processes across rewards and compensation, performance, learning, and onboarding. With rewards and compensation as your main focus, you’ll work with data and systems while gaining a broad understanding of how HR processes work across Ørsted.

As a team, we collaborate across locations and areas of expertise, share our knowledge, and support each other in learning and developing together.

You’ll play an important role in:

updating, validating, and analysing employee and rewards data, including eligibility and cost calculations
maintaining process documentation, guides, training materials, templates, and other supporting materials
supporting employees and people leaders with process-related questions and investigating data or system issues
contributing to process mapping and improvement by gathering user feedback, analysing data, and identifying opportunities to simplify and automate processes
collaborating with colleagues and stakeholders across People & Culture and other areas to coordinate data, information, and process activities.

To succeed in the role, you:

have strong Excel skills and enjoy working with numbers and data, including analysing information and using formulas to solve problems
have an analytical and curious mindset, with attention to detail and an interest in investigating and solving problems
are proactive and comfortable working independently, taking ownership of your tasks and identifying where you can contribute
communicate clearly in English and can build good working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders
are comfortable learning and working with different digital systems and are curious about how technology, automation, and AI can make processes simpler and more efficient.

Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply.

Shape the future with us
Send your application to us as soon as possible. We’ll be conducting interviews on a continuous basis and reserve the right to take down the advert when we’ve found the right candidate.

As an applicant or employee, you may request reasonable work and position accommodation or adjustments via accommodation@orsted.com.

Please note that this is a student position, and your employment will continue for as long as you meet the requirements for student employment.

Please note that for your application to be taken into consideration, you must submit your application via our online career pages and answer the screening questions relevant for your country. We don't take applications or inquiries from external recruiters or agencies into account for this position.

Position salary range:
For this position, the expected base pay range is kr165.00 per hour - kr185.00 per hour for the advertised location. The offered base salary will be determined within this range based on relevant skills, experience, and expected role fulfilment within the stated pay range to ensure a fair and competitive offer. Where applicable, you may also be eligible for variable payment and a comprehensive benefits package.

Our benefits package:
For this position, employees who meet eligibility requirements have access to: employer‑paid pension (11% contribution), full insurance coverage (accident, life, critical illness, and health insurance); five weeks of paid holiday plus 10 additional paid days off per holiday year; a 3% holiday allowance; access to Ørsted Life & Fitness Vitality including fitness classes, physiotherapy, massage, and wellbeing programmes; a multimedia package (mobile phone, PC, internet); staff club membership with sport and cultural activities; and access to the company canteen (monthly lunch scheme or daily tickets).

Pre-employment background check:
Certain positions may require a background check as part of the hiring process. If applicable, you will be informed during the recruitment process. Background checks are conducted by an external provider in accordance with local legal requirements.

Join a global leader in renewable energy

Ørsted is a global leader in offshore wind and is one of the largest renewable energy companies in the world. With us, you’ll play your part in creating a world that runs entirely on green energy. As a leading green energy company, we leverage the curiosity and passion of our people to innovate and develop new technologies or bring existing technologies to scale, collaborating with governments, suppliers, and our industry partners to make renewable energy solutions a reality. At Ørsted, we work together with openness and respect and seek fresh perspectives to solve any task at hand: big or small. 

About Ørsted


We provide countries, companies, and communities with sustainable, reliable, and cost-competitive energy solutions, including offshore and onshore wind, solar PV, and energy storage.
Our vision is to create a world that runs entirely on green energy.
We built the world’s first offshore wind farm, Vindeby in Denmark, in 1991, and completed the world’s largest, Hornsea 2 in the UK, in 2022.
We were founded in Denmark in 2006 and now have approximately 8,000 employees, working in 15 countries and counting. 

An inclusive team

At Ørsted, we strive to be an inclusive workplace where you’re respected for who you are, valued for the unique perspectives you bring, and rewarded fairly for what you achieve. We want all employees to have the same opportunities for impact and growth, no matter their age, race, ethnicity, place of birth, gender, sexual orientation, or disability.

About Ørsted

Ørsted is a global leader in developing, constructing, and operating offshore wind farms, with a core focus on Europe. Backed by 35 years of experience in offshore wind, Ørsted has 11.1 GW of installed offshore capacity and 7.2 GW under construction. Ørsted’s total installed renewable energy capacity spanning Europe, Asia Pacific, and North America exceeds 19.5 GW across a portfolio that also includes onshore wind, solar power, energy storage, bioenergy plants, and energy trading. Recognised as one of the world’s leading sustainable energy companies, Ørsted is guided by its vision of a world that runs entirely on green energy. Headquartered in Denmark, Ørsted employs approximately 7,200 people. Ørsted's shares are listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen (Orsted). In 2025, the group's operating profit excluding new partnerships and cancellation fees was DKK 25.1 billion (EUR 3.4 billion). Visit orsted.com or follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram.
